# Appeals, Parole, Pardons Appeals are handled by the Chief Justice. Attorneys may appeal a past ruling on behalf of their client, if presented with new evidence. If the evidence exonerates the Prisoner, their sentence is adjusted as necessary by the Chief Justice. A Prisoner sentenced to a Felony or Grand Felony crime may request an appeal by the Warden or Chief Justice, these appeals may be denied for any reason.
Prisoners may additionally receive parole per discretion of the Warden, CJ, or CO. Parolees are encouraged to seek gainful employment on station. Parolees may have any further criminal sentence escalated to permanent confinement regardless of severity.
A pardon may be issued to any Employee accused of any severity of crime, if deemed in the best interest of the crew and vessel, and when the circumstances of the defendant or their offense warrant a suspension of their sentence. Dire Emergencies may nullify the charges as outlined in the Extenuating circumstances of Crime Modifiers. A pardon may be issued by the Commanding Officer, Arresting Officer, Warden, or the Judge of a hearing and must be accompanied by an announcement, explaining who was pardoned, of what crime, and for what reason.
